features.name: gated_relative_load
features.code:
import numpy as np
import math

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Negative load relative to the mean load, but only where the job is large enough to matter; small jobs ignore load."""
    m = len(loads)
    mean = float(np.mean(loads))
    # scale of a typical past job (fallback to job itself)
    if len(past_jobs) > 0:
        typical = float(np.mean(past_jobs))
    else:
        typical = job if job > 0 else 1.0
    typical = max(typical, 1e-9)
    # how "big" this job is relative to typical: gate small jobs off
    ratio = job / typical
    gate = 1.0 - math.exp(-ratio)  # 0 for tiny jobs, ->1 for big ones
    # relative load deviation, normalized by typical scale
    denom = max(mean + job, typical, 1e-9)
    rel = (mean - loads) / denom  # positive for underloaded (good)
    return gate * rel
features.measures: Negative load relative to the mean load, but only where the job is large enough to matter; small jobs ignore load.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Negative shortfall of each machine below the mean load, scaled by the expected remaining job size (targets machines just under average when big jobs remain)."""
    m = len(loads)
    mean_load = float(np.mean(loads))
    # estimate typical remaining job size from history
    if past_jobs.size > 0:
        avg = float(np.mean(past_jobs))
    else:
        avg = job
    total_left = jobs_left * avg
    # expected final mean load if we place job on a machine this round is not needed;
    # shortfall relative to current mean, normalised by expected remaining spread
    scale = max(avg, 1e-9)
    shortfall = (mean_load - loads) / scale
    # how much headroom the future work implies: with lots of remaining work,
    # being under average matters more
    urgency = total_left / (total_left + m * max(mean_load, 1e-9) + 1e-9)
    vals = shortfall * (0.5 + 0.5 * urgency)
    return np.tanh(vals)
features.measures: Negative shortfall of each machine below the mean load, scaled by the expected remaining job size (targets machines just under average when big jobs remain).

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Estimated resulting makespan of this machine relative to a work-conserving ideal: (load+job) minus the average remaining work share."""
    m = len(loads)
    t = past_jobs.shape[0]
    # remaining work estimate: mean observed job size times jobs remaining (including current)
    if t > 0:
        mean_size = float(np.mean(past_jobs))
    else:
        mean_size = float(job)
    remaining_jobs = jobs_left + 1
    remaining_work = mean_size * remaining_jobs
    # ideal balanced final load from current total plus remaining work
    total_now = float(np.sum(loads))
    ideal_final = (total_now + remaining_work) / m
    new_load = loads + job
    # how much this machine would exceed the ideal final load if its extra share got smoothed
    excess = new_load - ideal_final
    scale = abs(ideal_final) + abs(job) + 1e-9
    return -excess / scale

features.code:
import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Load of each machine relative to the best (least-loaded) machine, rescaled by the spread of loads and blended with how close that machine is to overtaking the max load."""
    m = len(loads)
    lo = loads.min()
    hi = loads.max()
    span = hi - lo
    if span < 1e-12:
        span = 1.0
    # normalised position within the current load range: 0 for least loaded, 1 for most loaded
    pos = (loads - lo) / span
    # gap to the maximum load, in units of the arriving job: small gap => machine is nearly critical
    gap_to_max = (hi - loads) / (job + 1e-12)
    # combine: prefer machines that are low AND far from the max relative to the job size
    return np.tanh(pos + 1.0 / (1.0 + gap_to_max)) - pos
features.measures: Load of each machine relative to the best (least-loaded) machine, rescaled by the spread of loads and blended with how close that machine is to overtaking the max load.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Negative distance of each machine's post-placement load from the post-placement mean, scaled by the running spread of loads (std of current loads + job), so the pull toward the mean is stronger when loads are already uneven."""

    mean_post = (loads.sum() + job) / m

    spread = loads.std() + 1e-9
    values = -d / (spread + job / m + 1e-9)
    return values

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two columns: negated resulting makespan max(load+job, largest other load) and resulting load, each normalised by their own max."""
    x = loads + job
    m = loads.shape[0]
    if m == 1:
        M2 = -np.inf
    else:
        M2 = loads[np.argpartition(loads, -2)[-2]]
    M1 = loads.max()
    cnt = (loads == M1).sum()
    other = np.where((loads == M1) & (cnt == 1), M2, M1)
    R = np.maximum(x, other)
    col1 = -R / (R.max() + 1e-9)
    col2 = x / (x.max() + 1e-9)
    return np.stack([col1, col2], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two gated columns: big jobs spread to the emptiest machine (-normalised load), small jobs best-fit under the estimated final average T."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    xn = x / (x.max() + 1e-9)
    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0
    col_big = -xn
    col_small = np.where(x <= T, xn, -xn)
    return np.stack([big * col_big, (1.0 - big) * col_small], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Continuous size gate: big jobs spread to the emptiest machine, small jobs best-fit under final average T, blended by job/T ratio."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    xn = x / (x.max() + 1e-9)
    # continuous gate in [0,1]: how big is this job relative to the target final load
    g = job / (T + 1e-9)
    g = g / (1.0 + g)  # squash into (0,1), 0.5 at job==T
    # spread component: push to emptiest (negated normalised load)
    col_spread = -xn
    # fill component: best-fit under T, penalise overshoot above T
    over = np.maximum(xn - T / (x.max() + 1e-9), 0.0)
    col_fill = (xn - over) * (x <= T) + (-xn) * (x > T)
    return np.stack([g * col_spread, (1.0 - g) * col_fill], axis=1)
features.measures: Continuous size gate: big jobs spread to the emptiest machine, small jobs best-fit under final average T, blended by job/T ratio.

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Excess of a machine's resulting load over the ideal final load, but only penalised when this machine would itself become the bottleneck (post-load above the projected max of the others); otherwise rewards slack."""
    m = len(loads)
    t = past_jobs.shape[0]
    # remaining work estimate: mean observed job size times jobs remaining (including current)
    if t > 0:
        mean_size = float(np.mean(past_jobs))
    else:
        mean_size = float(job)
    remaining_jobs = jobs_left + 1
    remaining_work = mean_size * remaining_jobs
    total_now = float(np.sum(loads))
    ideal_final = (total_now + remaining_work) / m
    new_load = loads + job
    # projected max load among the *other* machines after this job
    other_max = np.max(np.where(np.arange(m)[:, None] == np.arange(m)[None, :], -np.inf, loads), axis=1)
    other_max = np.where(np.arange(m) == np.argmax(loads), np.sort(loads)[-2] if m > 1 else -np.inf, np.max(loads))
    # resulting makespan if we pick this machine
    resulting_mk = np.maximum(new_load, other_max)
    # the machine's own resulting load relative to ideal, and relative to the bottleneck it creates
    scale = abs(ideal_final) + abs(job) + 1e-9
    excess = (new_load - ideal_final) / scale
    # criticality: is this machine the one causing the makespan?
    critical = (new_load >= other_max).astype(float)
    # penalise excess when critical, reward slack (negative excess) always
    return -excess * (0.5 + 0.5 * critical)
features.measures: Excess of a machine's resulting load over the ideal final load, but only penalised when this machine would itself become the bottleneck (post-load above the projected max of the others); otherwise rewards slack.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Rank of each machine's load among all loads (0 = emptiest), scaled to [-1, 1], gated by job size vs estimated final average."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    if m <= 1:
        return np.zeros(m)
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    # rank of each load (ties get average-free ordinal via argsort of argsort)
    order = np.argsort(loads, kind="stable")
    ranks = np.empty(m)
    ranks[order] = np.arange(m)
    # normalise rank to [-1, 1]: emptiest -> -1, fullest -> +1
    r = (ranks / (m - 1)) * 2.0 - 1.0
    # for big jobs, prefer emptiest (negative r); small jobs mildly prefer fuller (positive r)
    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0
    return big * (-r) + (1.0 - big) * (0.5 * r)
features.measures: Rank of each machine's load among all loads (0 = emptiest), scaled to [-1, 1], gated by job size vs estimated final average.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Soft-gated by job size relative to remaining slack: big jobs spread (penalise loaded machines), small jobs fill the tightest machine still under the estimated final average T, with the gate blending smoothly and the fill term using headroom above the mean."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    total = loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past
    T = max(total / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    # spread column: mildly normalised negative load
    spread = -(x - x.mean()) / (T + 1e-9)
    # fill column: prefer machines whose post-load stays under T, more so the tighter they are
    head = T - x
    fill = head / (T + 1e-9)
    # smooth gate: how large is this job versus the typical remaining average scale
    scale = max(mean_past, T, 1e-9)
    g = job / (job + scale + 1e-9)
    return g * spread + (1.0 - g) * fill
features.measures: Soft-gated by job size relative to remaining slack: big jobs spread (penalise loaded machines), small jobs fill the tightest machine still under the estimated final average T, with the gate blending smoothly and the fill term using headroom above the mean.

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Three columns: smooth big/small gate g=clip(job/T,0,1) times spread-to-emptiest, plus (1-g) times fill-toward-T and (1-g) times overshoot-penalty."""

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two columns: tiny jobs avoid the r emptiest machines reserved for expected big jobs; plus normalised negative load."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mp = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    bigfrac = float(np.mean(past_jobs > 3.0 * mp)) if past_jobs.size else 0.0
    r = int(min(m // 2, max(0, round(jobs_left * bigfrac))))
    thr = np.sort(loads)[r - 1] if r >= 1 else -np.inf
    reserve = (loads <= thr).astype(float)
    small = 1.0 if job <= 0.2 * max(loads.max(), 1e-9) else 0.0

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Spread-vs-fill gate keyed to percentile of job among past jobs: big jobs spread to emptiest by margin over current min, small jobs best-fit toward T within a soft band."""
    m = loads.shape[0]

    spread = -(x - xmin) / rng

    overshoot = -np.maximum(0.0, x - T) / (T + 1e-9)

    big = pct

    col_over = (1.0 - big) * overshoot

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Three columns: big jobs spread to the emptiest machine (neg load rank); small jobs pack just under the projected final target T with a soft overshoot penalty; plus a column scoring slack of each machine below T after placement, weighted by how much the job itself fills that slack."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job

    # rank-based emptiness: 0 for the emptiest machine, 1 for the fullest (robust to scale)
    order = np.argsort(np.argsort(loads))
    rank_pos = order / max(m - 1, 1)
    col_big = -rank_pos  # spread big jobs to emptiest machines

    # small jobs: prefer a machine that lands just under T, soft-penalise overshoot
    slack = (T - x) / (T + 1e-9)             # positive = under target, negative = over
    col_small = np.tanh(3.0 * slack)          # smooth: near 1 when far under, ~0 at target, negative when over

    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0
    small = 1.0 - big

    # how much of the remaining slack this job consumes (fills gaps efficiently)
    gap_before = np.maximum(T - loads, 0.0) / (T + 1e-9)
    fill = 1.0 - np.abs(slack)              # 1 when exactly at target, decays with distance
    col_fill = small * gap_before * fill

    return np.stack([big * col_big, small * col_small, col_fill], axis=1)
features.measures: Three columns: big jobs spread to the emptiest machine (neg load rank); small jobs pack just under the projected final target T with a soft overshoot penalty; plus a column scoring slack of each machine below T after placement, weighted by how much the job itself fills that slack.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two columns: negative soft indicator that this machine becomes the unique bottleneck (sigmoid of excess over the largest other post-load), and negative excess measured against the projected final average T rather than the current max."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    post = loads + job
    # largest other post-load per candidate via prefix/suffix max
    pm = np.maximum.accumulate(post)
    sm = np.maximum.accumulate(post[::-1])[::-1]
    others = np.maximum(
        np.concatenate(([-np.inf], pm[:-1])),
        np.concatenate((sm[1:], [-np.inf])),
    )
    others = np.where(np.isfinite(others), others, post)
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    d = (post - others) / (T + 1e-9)
    soft_ind = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-4.0 * d))          # smooth bottleneck indicator
    excess_T = np.clip((post - np.maximum(others, T)) / (T + 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    return np.column_stack([-soft_ind, -excess_T])

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Lean-on-the-laggard: negative of load deviation from the mean, but steepened by how far this machine sits below the running minimum load, so picking an already-light machine is rewarded superlinearly when the job is large relative to the spread."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mu = loads.mean()
    dev = loads - mu
    spread = (loads.max() - loads.min())
    spread = spread if spread > 1e-9 else 1e-9
    # how far below the mean, normalised by the current spread (in [-1, 0] for light machines)
    below = -dev / spread
    # size of the arriving job relative to the current load spread
    r = job / (spread + job + 1e-9)
    # baseline term (same spirit as parent) plus a convex bonus for laggards
    base = -dev / (mu + job + 1e-9)
    bonus = r * (below ** 2) * (below > 0)
    return base + bonus

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Negative squared excess of this machine's post-load over the second-largest post-load, gated to only fire when this machine becomes the unique max, plus a column measuring how much the new max exceeds the pre-existing max load."""
    n = loads.shape[0]
    post = loads + job

    order = np.argsort(post)
    largest = post[order[-1]]
    second = post[order[-2]] if n >= 2 else 0.0

    is_max = (post >= largest - 1e-12).astype(float)

    pre_max = loads.max()
    col2 = -np.clip((post - pre_max) / (pre_max + job + 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    return np.column_stack([col1, col2])

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):

        second = x[order[-2]]

    neg = np.minimum(d, 0.0)
    return np.stack([pos - 0.5 * neg, -(pos ** 2) + 0.25 * (neg ** 2)], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Big jobs spread toward emptiest under projected target T; small jobs fill toward T ranked by projected slack to T with a relative-to-mean smoothing."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    remaining = jobs_left * mean_past
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + remaining) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    scale = max(T, 1e-9)

    # big jobs: how far this machine's post-load sits above the projected target (spread the tall ones)
    overshoot = (x - T) / scale
    col_big = -overshoot

    # small jobs: prefer machines whose post-load stays under T, but prefer higher post-load among those
    # (best-fit under target); soft hinge so just-under-T is best, penalise overshoot along the way
    slack = (T - x) / scale
    col_small = slack - np.maximum(slack, 0.0) * 0.0  # slack itself: closer to T (smaller positive slack) scores... 
    # we want best-fit: maximize x among x<=T -> minimize slack for positive slack, and strongly penalise negative slack
    col_small = -np.abs(slack) - np.maximum(-slack, 0.0) * 3.0

    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0
    return np.stack([big * col_big, (1.0 - big) * col_small], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """For each machine: the projected idle time it will carry to the end if it receives this job, estimated as max(T_final - (load+job), 0) minus the same quantity averaged over machines, normalised by T_final; big jobs get this signal suppressed and instead see a negative quadratic penalty on how far above the least-loaded machine they land."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    if past_jobs.size:
        mean_past = past_jobs.mean()
        p90 = np.percentile(past_jobs, 90)
    else:
        mean_past = job
        p90 = job
    # Projected final average load including the arriving job and expected remaining work.
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    # Expected residual idle if this machine ends up at x and the rest average T:
    idle = np.maximum(T - x, 0.0)
    idle_centered = idle - idle.mean()
    # Normalise: relative to typical remaining horizon.
    spread_scale = max(T, p90, 1e-9)
    col_idle = idle_centered / spread_scale

    big_thresh = max(T, p90)
    is_big = 1.0 if job >= big_thresh else 0.0
    if is_big:

        over = np.maximum(x - lmin, 0.0) / spread_scale
        col_big = -(over ** 2)

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Gated columns: big jobs spread to emptiest scaled by urgency of remaining work; small jobs best-fit ranked by slack-to-T, both weighted by how tight T is versus the current max."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    var_past = past_jobs.var() if past_jobs.size > 1 else 0.0
    total = loads.sum() + job
    T = max((total + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    xmax = x.max() + 1e-9
    xn = x / xmax

    # urgency: how much headroom the projected target has over current max load
    # (small => tight, big jobs matter more)
    slack_T = max(T - loads.max(), 0.0) / (T + 1e-9)
    urgency = 1.0 / (1.0 + slack_T)  # in (0, 1], near 1 when tight

    # uncertainty of the target from past-job variance
    unc = np.sqrt(var_past + 1e-9) / (mean_past + 1e-9)
    unc = unc / (1.0 + unc)

    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0

    # big jobs: spread to emptiest, but penalise leaving a machine far below mean
    # (avoid stranding the emptiest too far under, since a big tail is coming)
    col_big = -xn * urgency - (1.0 - urgency) * (x / (xmean := (x.mean() + 1e-9)))

    # small jobs: best-fit under T, with a soft slack term that grows with uncertainty
    slack = (T - x) / (T + 1e-9)  # positive if under target
    col_small = np.where(x <= T, xn * (1.0 - 0.5 * unc), -xn) + 0.3 * unc * slack

    return np.stack([big * col_big, (1.0 - big) * col_small], axis=1)

    """Three columns: hinge of each machine's post-load above the largest *other* post-load, expressed (a) relative to projected target T, (b) relative to the current load spread (so only near-ties penalised), (c) the same excess diluted by how many jobs are left (early ties less critical)."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    x = loads + job
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)

    if m == 1:
        sec = np.zeros(1)
    else:
        order = np.argsort(x)
        largest = x[order[-1]]
        second = x[order[-2]]
        sec = np.full(m, largest)
        sec[order[-1]] = second

    excess = np.maximum(x - sec, 0.0)

    # (a) scaled by projected target
    e_t = excess / (T + 1e-9)
    # (b) scaled by current load spread (how much of the existing imbalance this excess represents)
    spread = max(loads.max() - loads.min(), 1e-9) if m > 1 else 1e-9
    e_s = excess / (spread + job + 1e-9)
    # (c) same excess, but shrunk when many jobs remain (a lone early lead is harmless)
    shrink = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.sqrt(max(jobs_left, 0)) / max(m, 1))
    e_l = e_t * shrink

    return np.stack([-e_t, -e_s, -e_l], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two columns: -std(loads)/scale for tiny jobs (balance first), and a load-squared deficit term for large jobs, gated by job vs typical size."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    if past_jobs.size:
        med = np.median(past_jobs)
        mean_past = past_jobs.mean()
    else:
        med = job
        mean_past = job
    med = max(med, 1e-9)
    mean_past = max(mean_past, 1e-9)
    # projected final target
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)

    x = loads + job
    # size gate: how large is this job relative to the typical (median) past job
    g = np.clip(job / (job + med), 0.0, 1.0)

    # column A (small jobs): prefer machines whose post-load sits closest to the
    # *median* post-load, i.e. mild balance toward the middle, not the min.
    spread = x.std() + 1e-9
    mid = np.median(x)
    col_small = -np.abs(x - mid) / (spread * m) 

    # column B (large jobs): penalise the machine whose post-load squared excess
    # over the projected average T is largest (superlinear crowding penalty),
    # plus a mild pull to the emptiest.
    over = np.maximum(x - T, 0.0) / (T + 1e-9)
    col_big = -(over ** 2) - 0.1 * (x / (T + 1e-9))

    return np.stack([(1.0 - g) * col_small, g * col_big], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Three columns: -e and -e^2 with e = max(x - sec,0)/T (as before), plus a column that rewards the machine whose post-load x is closest to T from below, weighted by how much of the gap-to-T the job fills (fill-efficiency), scaled to [-1,1]."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    x = loads + job
    total = loads.sum()
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((total + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)

    if m == 1:
        sec = np.zeros(1)
    else:
        order = np.argsort(x)
        largest = x[order[-1]]
        second = x[order[-2]]
        sec = np.full(m, largest)
        sec[order[-1]] = second

    e = np.maximum(x - sec, 0.0) / (T + 1e-9)

    # Fill-efficiency column: prefer machines that end near T without overshooting,
    # and among those prefer the one that was emptier before (larger job share).
    # s = projected slack to T after placement, normalized by T.
    s = (T - x) / (T + 1e-9)              # >0 = under target, <0 = over target
    # penalise overshoot strongly, reward being just under T
    fill = np.where(s >= 0.0, s, 2.0 * s) / (1.0 + np.abs(s))
    # empty-machine preference: share of this job in the machine's new load
    share = job / (x + 1e-9)
    col_fill = np.tanh(3.0 * fill) * (0.5 + 0.5 * share)

    return np.stack([-e, -(e ** 2), col_fill], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Small-job column scores by headroom to a per-machine soft ceiling (T minus fill), big-job column by negative load relative to the largest load; both scaled by how tight T is vs the biggest current load."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    total = loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past
    T = max(total / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    xmax = max(x.max(), 1e-9)

    # tightness: how close the projected average is to the largest post-load
    # (near 1 when one machine already dominates the eventual average)
    tight = T / xmax

    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0

    # big jobs: spread, but penalise the machine that would become the unique max
    # more strongly when the schedule is already tight
    col_big = -(x / xmax) * (1.0 + tight)

    # small jobs: soft-ceiling fill. Score = headroom below T, but only for machines
    # already under T; machines above T get a graded penalty proportional to overshoot.
    over = np.maximum(x - T, 0.0) / (T + 1e-9)
    under = np.maximum(T - x, 0.0) / (T + 1e-9)
    col_small = under - 2.0 * over

    return np.stack([big * col_big, (1.0 - big) * col_small], axis=1)
features.measures: Small-job column scores by headroom to a per-machine soft ceiling (T minus fill), big-job column by negative load relative to the largest load; both scaled by how tight T is vs the biggest current load.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two columns: -e*w and -(e^2)*w, where e is the normalised excess of a machine's post-load over the second-largest post-load and w discounts it by the fraction of other machines that remaining work can still lift above it."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job

    if m == 1:
        sec = np.zeros(1)
    else:
        order = np.argsort(x)
        largest = order[-1]
        second = x[order[-2]]
        sec = np.full(m, second)
        sec[largest] = x[order[-2]]

    e = np.maximum(x - sec, 0.0) / T

    rem = jobs_left * mean_past / m
    reach = loads[None, :] + rem >= x[:, None]  # reach[i, j]: machine j can reach x[i]
    count = reach.sum(axis=1) - reach[np.arange(m), np.arange(m)]
    if m > 1:
        w = 1.0 - np.clip(count / (m - 1), 0.0, 1.0)
    else:
        w = np.ones(m)

    return np.stack([-e * w, -(e * e) * w], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Gated columns: big jobs ranked by negative post-load excess over the projected floor; small jobs ranked by signed distance below/above a soft target T, using both linear and squared (two-sided) forms."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    xmax = x.max() + 1e-9
    xn = x / xmax
    Tn = T / xmax

    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0

    # Big: spread to emptiest relative to projected floor; penalise pushing above it.
    excess = np.maximum(xn - Tn, 0.0)
    col_big_lin = -xn
    col_big_pen = -(excess ** 2)

    # Small: pack just under T. Below T we like bigger fill (reward xn), above T we dislike (penalty grows quadratically).
    d = xn - Tn
    col_small_fill = np.where(d <= 0.0, xn, -xn)
    col_small_sq = -(d ** 2)

    return np.stack([
        big * col_big_lin,
        big * col_big_pen,
        (1.0 - big) * col_small_fill,
        (1.0 - big) * col_small_sq,
    ], axis=1)
features.measures: Gated columns: big jobs ranked by negative post-load excess over the projected floor; small jobs ranked by signed distance below/above a soft target T, using both linear and squared (two-sided) forms.

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Tiny-job hard-cap hinge: for jobs small vs the projected final average, reward machines whose post-load stays under the largest current load (slack to the cap), penalise those that exceed it, scaled by how much slack remains to the projected target."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    Lmax = float(loads.max())

    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    # tiny relative to the projected target (scale-free, unlike a cap on raw load)
    tiny = 1.0 if job <= 0.1 * T else 0.0

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Fraction of remaining projected work that would exceed T if this job lands here, gated by how large the job is relative to the mean."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    total_after = loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past
    T = max(total_after / m, 1e-9)

    col2 = -gate * (exc ** 2)

    col3 = gate * slack

    return np.stack([col1, col2, col3], axis=1)

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two columns: per-machine load centred on the running min+max midpoint, then gated by whether the job fills that machine toward the projected final target T (tighter near the floor, wider above)."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job

    # under-target machines get reward, over-target penalised, saturating
    fill = np.tanh(-d)
    return np.stack([c * fill, c * (1.0 - np.abs(fill))], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two gated columns measured in units of the remaining jobs' projected work per machine: big jobs spread by negative slack below the projected ceiling, small jobs best-fit against slack to the current mean, all relative to the spread of loads."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    total_proj = loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past
    T = max(total_proj / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    # spread of loads sets a natural scale; fall back to T
    scale = max(loads.std(), 1e-9) if loads.size else T
    scale = max(scale, 0.1 * T)

    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0

    # big: spreading reward proportional to how far a machine sits above the projected average,
    # measured in load-spread units (so crowding relative to current imbalance matters).
    col_big = -np.tanh((x - T) / scale)

    # small: best-fit where post-load lands closest to (but not far under) the current mean,
    # scored with a signed distance in load-spread units, sign flipped so under-mean is preferred
    # but with a soft cap so very empty machines are not over-rewarded.
    cur_mean = max(loads.mean(), 1e-9)
    col_small = -np.tanh((x - cur_mean) / scale)

    return np.stack([big * col_big, (1.0 - big) * col_small], axis=1)

import numpy as np
import math

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two columns: negative excess of post-load above a soft ceiling that shrinks with expected count of future big jobs (hinge and squared hinge), normalised by projected final average."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job

    # Estimate size and arrival rate of "big" jobs from history
    if past_jobs.size >= 20:
        thr = np.quantile(past_jobs, 0.95)
        big = past_jobs[past_jobs >= thr]
        S = float(big.mean()) if big.size else float(past_jobs.max())
        b_rate = big.size / past_jobs.size
    else:
        S = float(past_jobs.max()) if past_jobs.size else job
        b_rate = 0.0
    S = max(S, 1e-9)

    # Expected number of future big jobs still to arrive, spread across machines
    exp_big = jobs_left * b_rate
    per_machine = exp_big / m
    # Ceiling = current max load lowered by expected future big-job pressure,
    # but never below the current mean load (can't go below what's needed to balance).
    C = float(loads.max())
    shift = S * min(per_machine, 1.0)
    R = max(C - shift, float(loads.mean()))

    excess = np.maximum(x - R, 0.0) / T
    return np.stack([-excess, -(excess ** 2)], axis=1)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Slack of each machine to the projected final average T, measured relative to the largest job still expected to arrive."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    # expected size of the largest remaining job grows with the spread of past sizes
    if past_jobs.size >= 2:
        sd = past_jobs.std()
        big_est = max(mean_past + 2.0 * sd, job)
    else:
        big_est = max(job, mean_past)
    x = loads + job
    # a machine far below T can absorb a future big job: reward slack up to big_est, saturate beyond
    slack = np.clip((T - x) / (big_est + 1e-9), -1.0, 1.0)
    return slack

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Per-machine centred load deficit scaled by a size-gated factor: strongly favours the emptiest machine for big jobs, but only mildly for small jobs, relative to the current load spread."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    T = max((loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    # spread of current loads, a natural unit for how much room a machine has

    # a huge job flattens the ranking (all machines look similarly empty) while
    # small jobs sharpen it
    denom = max(spread, job, 1e-9)

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Gated two columns: big-job arrivals rank by free headroom below a future-lowered ceiling (higher = safer), small jobs rank by how far their post-load sits below the projected floor, scaled by remaining-work slack."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    total_now = loads.sum() + job
    T = max((total_now + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job

    # estimate the typical and extreme future job sizes from history
    if past_jobs.size >= 20:
        thr = np.quantile(past_jobs, 0.95)
        big = past_jobs[past_jobs >= thr]
        S = float(big.mean()) if big.size else float(past_jobs.max())
        b_rate = big.size / past_jobs.size
    else:
        S = float(past_jobs.max()) if past_jobs.size else job
        b_rate = 0.0
    S = max(S, 1e-9)

    # remaining-work slack: how much future volume is likely still to come
    rem = jobs_left * mean_past
    urgency = rem / (rem + total_now + 1e-9)  # in (0,1)

    # ceiling that future big jobs will push up toward: current max is a floor of it
    C = float(loads.max())
    expected_big_rise = S * min(jobs_left * b_rate / m, 1.0)
    R = max(C - 0.5 * expected_big_rise * (1.0 - urgency), float(loads.mean()))

    # big-job column: headroom below the (lowered) ceiling, only meaningful for big arrivals
    headroom = (R - x) / T
    col_big = np.clip(headroom, -1.0, 1.0)

    # small-job column: signed distance below projected floor, weighted by urgency
    floor = T
    below = np.clip((floor - x) / T, -1.0, 1.0)
    col_small = below * (0.5 + 0.5 * urgency)

    big_gate = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0
    return np.stack([big_gate * col_big, (1.0 - big_gate) * col_small], axis=1)
features.measures: Gated two columns: big-job arrivals rank by free headroom below a future-lowered ceiling (higher = safer), small jobs rank by how far their post-load sits below the projected floor, scaled by remaining-work slack.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Two gated columns: big jobs spread by squared slack-to-T, small jobs fill toward T weighted by remaining work pressure."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = past_jobs.mean() if past_jobs.size else job
    total_proj = loads.sum() + job + jobs_left * mean_past
    T = max(total_proj / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    # remaining work pressure: 1 when lots to come, shrinking as horizon ends
    pressure = jobs_left / (jobs_left + 1.0)
    big = 1.0 if job >= T else 0.0
    # big: prefer machines far below target (squared slack), scaled by pressure
    slack = np.clip((T - x) / (T + 1e-9), -1.0, 1.0)
    col_big = pressure * slack * np.abs(slack) + (1.0 - pressure) * (-x / (x.max() + 1e-9))
    # small: fill toward T, softer below, harder penalty above; scaled by pressure
    below = np.clip((T - x) / (T + 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    above = np.clip((x - T) / (T + 1e-9), 0.0, 1.0)
    col_small = pressure * (below - 1.5 * above) + (1.0 - pressure) * (-x / (x.max() + 1e-9))
    return np.stack([big * col_big, (1.0 - big) * col_small], axis=1)
features.measures: Two gated columns: big jobs spread by squared slack-to-T, small jobs fill toward T weighted by remaining work pressure.

import numpy as np

def feature(job, loads, past_jobs, jobs_left):
    """Negative post-load plus per-machine expected future big-job reserve, gated to small jobs and scaled to [-1, 1]."""
    m = loads.shape[0]
    mean_past = float(past_jobs.mean()) if past_jobs.size else float(job)
    T = max((float(loads.sum()) + job + jobs_left * mean_past) / m, 1e-9)
    x = loads + job
    med = float(np.median(past_jobs)) if past_jobs.size else mean_past
    thr = max(5.0 * med, 0.25 * T)
    if past_jobs.size:
        big = past_jobs >= thr
        n_big = int(big.sum())
        rate = n_big / float(past_jobs.size)
        mean_big = float(past_jobs[big].mean()) if n_big else thr
    else:
        rate, mean_big = 0.0, thr
    exp_future = rate * jobs_left * mean_big          # total expected future big load
    g = exp_future / (exp_future + T)                 # 0 when no monster has been seen
    free = loads < thr                                # machine carries no big job yet
    n_free = max(int(free.sum()), 1)
    reserve = np.where(free, exp_future / n_free, 0.0)
    small = 1.0 if job < thr else 0.0
    col = -g * small * (x + reserve) / (T + float(reserve.max()))
    return col.reshape(-1, 1)

    """Negative excess of each machine's post-load over the mean of the k=min(3,m-1) largest other post-loads, normalised by projected final average."""

nodes.title: bottleneck-avoidance
nodes.description: Penalise any placement that makes this machine the unique new maximum load, scaled by how far above the second-largest load it lands.

nodes.title: wide find: rank_emptiness_scaled_by_job_vs_imbalance
nodes.description: Ratio of the job to the spread (max-min) of loads, times the rank of the machine's emptiness: rewards tall-but-empty machines when the job is huge relative to the current imbalance.

notes.result: not attempted: no feature under it is close to a duplicate or to the kept features (nearest rho < 0.93, R^2 < 0.98)

nodes.title: smooth-makespan-surrogate
nodes.description: Score each candidate by the increase it causes in a log-sum-exp (soft-max) of the post-placement loads, normalised by the projected final average, so the top of the load profile dominates nonlinearly.

nodes.title: endgame-switch
nodes.description: Gate between balance-seeking behaviour and pure lowest-post-load as jobs_left shrinks (mirror start-up gate), so the final max is optimised only when the horizon is nearly over.

nodes.title: big-job-spread-by-rank
nodes.description: For jobs large relative to running mean, spread by rank of emptiness (not absolute load), since loads are dominated by tiny jobs.

nodes.title: bottleneck-vs-remaining-big-jobs
nodes.description: Penalise becoming the unique max scaled by how many big jobs are still expected to arrive (jobs_left times past big-job rate).

nodes.title: bottleneck-count-pressure
nodes.description: Penalise becoming the unique max scaled by how many machines sit near the max (ties dilute the penalty), so the policy avoids creating a lone tall machine when others could share.

nodes.title: big-job-slot-reservation
nodes.description: For big jobs, prefer machines with fewest big jobs already, reserving lightly-loaded machines for the expected remaining big jobs.

nodes.title: wide find: median_balance_vs_quadratic_overshoot
nodes.description: Two columns: -std(loads)/scale for tiny jobs (balance first), and a load-squared deficit term for large jobs, gated by job vs typical size.

nodes.title: packing-occupancy
nodes.description: Score machines by how well a small job fills existing idle capacity (occupancy/fit) rather than by load balance, so tiny jobs pack onto busy machines instead of spreading.

argued.argument: Two-sided quadratic hinge around Lmax is not a monotone transform of f011's linear best-fit column; gating and curvature differ, so no span/duplicate certificate holds.

notes.result: not proven: stays at lower priority

nodes.title: big-job-slot-count
nodes.description: Count big jobs already placed per machine and prefer machines with fewer big-job slots used, independent of load, to keep big-job capacity available in bimodal.

nodes.title: wide find: size_rank_quartile_gate_spread_vs_fill
nodes.description: Spread-vs-fill gated by the job's size rank among past jobs (big = top-quartile size), using post-load relative to projected target.

nodes.title: remaining-big-job-count-gate
nodes.description: Gate the spread/fill mix on the expected number of remaining big jobs (jobs_left times past big-job rate) rather than on the arriving job's size, so the policy reserves slots while big jobs are still coming.

nodes.title: bimodal-idle-fill
nodes.description: For tiny jobs, score machines by how much of their idle capacity a small job closes without lifting the projected floor, targeting the bimodal family's 36% idle.

nodes.title: future-big-slot-reservation
nodes.description: Add each machine's expected future big-job load (remaining big-job rate times mean big size, split over the big-job-free machines) to its post-load, so small jobs fill machines that already carry a big job.

nodes.title: quantile-fill-target
nodes.description: For tiny jobs, replace the mean fill target with an upper quantile of current loads, so jobs top up already-loaded machines instead of piling onto the few big-job-free ones.

nodes.title: dispersion-gated-fill
nodes.description: Gate small-job fill on the relative spread of loads: fill toward the mean only when loads are tight, switch to spread/lowest-load when a few machines dominate.
